newsitem.title: USA: AMD chips selected for IBM PCs.
newsitem.headline: AMD chips selected for IBM PCs.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc., rival chipmaker of industry giant Intel Corp., said Monday International Business Machines Corp. will use AMD's new K6 MMX microprocessor in some of its Aptiva personal computers.
Terms were not disclosed, but news of the deal sent AMD shares sharply higher to end up $4 at $41.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"This relationship further validates the growing acceptance and value of the AMD-K6 processor," Vinod Dham, vice president of AMD's Computation Products Group, said in a statement.
IBM will announce which products will use the K6 processor in the future, AMD said.
AMD, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., had revenues of $2 billion in 1996.
